title: Prompt engineering: instructions, few-shot, and output contracts
summary: Write prompts that behave like reliable function calls: clear instructions, well-chosen examples, and an output shape your code can trust.

title: Context engineering: what actually goes into the window
summary: Prompt engineering asks how to phrase the request — context engineering asks what the model gets to see. The attention-budget mental model, the write/select/compress/isolate toolkit, and the five failure modes that break agents.

title: RAG architectures: naive, advanced, and when to skip RAG
summary: Don't teach the model your data — hand it the right pages at query time. Chunking, hybrid search, reranking, groundedness gates — and knowing when to skip RAG entirely.

title: Chunking and embeddings: the unglamorous 80%
summary: The two unglamorous decisions that determine 80% of retrieval quality: how you cut documents into self-contained chunks, and how you turn them into vectors. Cosine similarity as an angle, the one-model rule, and the token-level eval that keeps chunking honest.

title: Vector databases: indexes, ANN search, and trade-offs
summary: Your embeddings are points in space; finding the nearest ones is the retrieval problem. Why exact search dies at scale, how HNSW and IVF make ANN fast, and the recall–latency–memory triangle every index trades on.

title: Re-ranking and query rewriting for retrieval quality
summary: Retrieval fails at two ends: a bad probe and a coarse ranker. Sharpen the query (rewrite, HyDE, multi-query) then re-score a small candidate set with a cross-encoder: cheap and wide first, precise and narrow second.

title: Knowledge graphs for RAG (GraphRAG patterns)
summary: Vector RAG finds strings that look similar; GraphRAG answers questions about things that are connected. Extract entities and relationships, cluster them into summarized communities, then answer by local fan-out or global map-reduce — with every claim citing its source.

title: Tool calling / function calling done right
summary: The model never runs your code — it just asks. Give the LLM a JSON-schema tool menu, let it emit structured calls, and let your code validate, execute, and loop on tool_result.

title: Structured outputs: JSON mode, grammars, and validation
summary: The schema-shaped hole cut into the decoder: constrained decoding masks invalid tokens before sampling, so output is schema-valid by construction — plus strict mode's three rules, the Pydantic pattern, and why shape is never truth.

title: Agent memory systems: short-term, long-term, episodic
summary: A model has no memory between turns — so memory is a system you build around it: the context window as the desk (short-term), a namespace-scoped store as the filing cabinet (semantic facts, episodic experiences, procedural rules), and the two policies that are the whole craft — what to write and how to read it back.

title: Planning and reasoning: CoT, ReAct, tree-of-thought
summary: There is no silent thinking inside an LLM — the scratchpad is the thinking. CoT spends tokens on intermediate steps, ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so the world corrects the chain, and tree-of-thought stops betting on a single chain and searches instead.

title: Multi-agent orchestration and handoffs
summary: A team of agents is an organizational design problem, not a model problem: split work only for genuine parallelism or isolated context, pick the topology by who owns the final answer, hand off with a written memo, keep one writer — and put the 15x token bill on the eval scorecard.

title: LLM evals and LLM-as-judge: building trust in outputs
summary: You can't improve what you can't measure — and stochastic outputs need measuring differently. Error analysis tells you which evals to write, code graders catch the objective failures, an LLM judge grades the subjective ones — but the judge stays on probation until it agrees with humans.

title: Eval-driven development for AI features
summary: TDD's red-green loop for AI features: define "good" as a labeled dataset of tasks plus graders before any prompt, model, or tooling change; score every change in CI; harvest production failures into the suite.

title: Fine-tuning vs RAG vs prompting: how to choose
summary: Three levers, three different jobs: prompting steers behavior in-session, RAG supplies fresh facts, fine-tuning bakes in style and task format. The ladder order, the dataset bar, the cost math — and how to combine them.

title: Guardrails, safety, and prompt-injection defense
summary: Prompt injection is LLM01 on the OWASP Top 10 because instructions and data share one text channel. Assume the injection succeeds and make success harmless: least privilege, input/output guardrails, gated tools, and human confirmation for irreversible actions.

title: Inference optimization: quantization, vLLM, batching
summary: Serving an LLM is a memory-bandwidth problem: shrink weights with quantization, kill KV-cache waste with PagedAttention, and keep the GPU busy with continuous batching.

title: Streaming UX for AI products
summary: Streaming trades total wait for perceived wait: first tokens in under a second, partial markdown rendered safely, and a stream state machine that treats drops and stops as normal.

title: Semantic caching to cut cost and latency
summary: Stop paying full token price for rephrased questions: embed each prompt, match it against cached answers by meaning, and skip the LLM call entirely — plus the threshold, TTL, and key-scoping rules that keep the cache honest.

title: Model routing, fallbacks, and cost control
summary: Stop hard-coding providers: route a logical model name across deployments by strategy, fail over through ordered backups, and hard-cap spend with per-key budgets.

title: Distillation: small models from big ones
summary: Train a small student to imitate a big teacher: soft targets and temperature (white-box), teacher generations (black-box), the T-squared loss formula, prune-then-distill — and why students shine on narrow tasks but keep an imitation gap on broad reasoning.

title: Synthetic data generation for training and evals
summary: Labeled data is the bottleneck: generate it with an LLM instead. Seed-anchored generation, diversity controls, judge-and-filter pipelines, and decontamination — the recipe for synthetic training and eval datasets you can actually trust.

title: Observability for LLM apps: traces, token accounting
summary: Stop debugging your AI app with a stopwatch: model every request as a trace, capture gen_ai.* attributes and token counts on every span, and alert on cost, latency, and errors.

title: State machines for agents: explicit states beat vibes
summary: A prompt-then-tool-call chain has no concept of where it is or what to do when a step fails. Name every state, declare the allowed transitions, make failure a first-class node, and persist state at each transition — resumable, auditable agents.

title: Workflow orchestration engines: durable execution that survives crashes
summary: A multi-step agent that dies at step 7 loses everything. Durable execution records every step's result in an event history, so a fresh worker replays that history and resumes exactly where the crash stopped — retries declared in config, not in code.
